title: Rome: remitted sins' stain wiped, yet vicious habits remain to be deleted
source_text: XXVIII. Deinde quamvis dicant Scholae Romanae Theologi in eo qui justificatur peccata tolli & aboleri prorsus, & quum peccata a Deo remittuntur relictam ex iis maculam totam elui: attamen non negant habitus vitiosos per actualia peccata contractos, etiam post illa remissa remanere, vique & auxilio gratiae divinae paulatim delendos & abolendos esse, eaque in re ex parte consistere fidelium in virtute & sanctificatione progressum, ut videre est apud Bellarminum de Amissione gratiae & statu peccati, lib. 1. cap. 13.
pass_a_gloss: Next, although the Theologians of the Roman School say that in the one who is justified sins are utterly taken away and abolished, and that when sins are remitted by God the whole stain left from them is washed away: yet they do not deny that vicious habits contracted through actual sins remain even after those are remitted, and are to be deleted and abolished gradually by the force and help of divine grace, and that in that matter in part consists the progress of the faithful in virtue and sanctification, as may be seen in Bellarmine On the Loss of Grace and the State of Sin, book 1, chapter 13.
pass_b_english: Rome says remission wipes the whole leftover stain, yet admits vicious habits remain after remitted acts.
Those habits are slowly deleted by grace—and that is part of sanctification progress (Bellarmine).

lemmas.gloss: the whole stain is washed away
